name: Electricity
summary: Burn lava for Forge Energy, carry it on Power Lines, store it in Batteries and turn it back into rotation with Electric Motors.

teach.what: A complete FE grid inside the mod: the [[lava-generator]] and [[geothermal-turbine]] make Forge Energy, [[power-lines|Power Lines]] carry it, [[battery|Batteries]] store it, and the [[electric-motor]] turns it into Create rotation of up to 294,912 SU.
teach.why: Rotation is hard to move long distances and hard to make in huge amounts. FE travels any distance on a thin cable, and one motor can match a full superheated steam boiler. It also powers [[trade-bot|Trade Bot]] and the [[netherite-monster-cage]].
teach.when: Once you have brass, Industrial Iron and a lava supply (a [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]]). The turbine and Industrial Battery come later, as grid projects.
teach.interacts: Fuel comes from the [[fluid-wellspring]] on [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]]. Pipez energy pipes and other mods' FE blocks connect too: anything that gives or takes FE through a face works.
mistakes: Leaving generators with nothing to power. They always run flat out while fuelled; what isn't used fills stores and the rest is lost.
Running a big motor on copper cable. Copper carries 4,096 FE a tick: enough for 65,536 SU of motor at most.
Feeding a Lava Generator from its side. Lava goes in at the middle of its back; power comes out of its sides.
Expecting a motor to limp along when short of power. It stops, then restarts once it has a reserve stored.

sections.title: Making FE
body: Two generators burn lava. Both run **flat out** whenever they have fuel: there's no throttle on the Lava Generator, and the Geothermal Turbine runs at whatever power level you set on it with a Wrench, in 10% steps.

head: Takes
Gives
FE per mB of lava
rows: 20 mB/s lava, in at the middle of the back
1,024 FE a tick, out of each side's terminal
90 mB/s lava and 250 mB/s water, through the ports under its base
46,080 FE a tick, through the ports under its base

body: The turbine is ten times as efficient with lava. Build it as a 3x3x3 of Geothermal Casings with a Turbine Core in the very middle and the Controller in the middle of the front, facing you; it forms within a second.

body.tip: Lava Generators whose side terminals touch share their stored FE, so a cable on any one of them draws on the whole row.

body.warning: What a generator's own store can't hold is lost. Give it a machine or a Battery to fill.

sections.title: Turning FE into rotation
body: The [[electric-motor]] takes FE through its base (the flange opposite the shaft) and turns its shaft at the speed and stress you set with a Wrench. Speed snaps to Create's standard speeds from 1 to 256 RPM; stress snaps to what the generators make (a quarter or half of a Lava Generator, whole generators, up to one turbine), and the screen shows the power it will draw.

head: Motor set to
Draws
Lava Generators' worth
rows: 294,912 SU (its maximum: a full superheated boiler)

body: The rule is simple: **1 FE a tick for every 16 SU**.

Short of power, a motor stops, and starts again once it has a reserve stored (30 seconds' worth, or a few seconds' at high stress). A weak supply makes it pause now and then rather than stutter the whole network.

body.fact: Running a motor at its full 294,912 SU earns Unlimited Power: "A whole steam boiler, from one block".

sections.title: Storing FE
body: A [[battery]] stores 10,000,000 FE, in or out at 2,048 FE a tick. On a network it fills from what the generators make beyond what's used, and gives it back when they fall short. That's about 8 minutes of one Lava Generator's output, or a full-power motor for about 27 seconds: storage evens out supply, it doesn't replace generation.

list: Its connectors are its sides, front and back. Batteries that touch there are one **bank** with one store, moving 2,048 FE a tick each. Stacked ones don't join.

Fill a 3x3 footprint, 3 to 9 high, and they form one **Industrial Battery**: 20,000,000 FE a block (540 million at 3 high, 1.62 billion at 9). It connects only through the four insulators on its top corners, by spans to [[line-post|Line Posts]].
A Lightning Rod on top adds 250,000 FE a strike.
Broken or picked up, a Battery keeps its charge. Breaking a tower block re-forms the tallest run of 3 or more full layers left; nothing is lost.

body.tip: Once a tower stands, a Battery placed on its top fills the whole 3x3 layer from your stack (nine at once), so it grows like a Create vault.

sections.title: Far away: generators on paper
body: A Power Line network is a lasting record of its generators and devices. A device is **live** while its chunk is running, and each tick the network sets live devices' use against its generators' output.

A generator whose chunk isn't running carries on **on paper** from its record: its output, store, fuel, and what its Wellsprings bring in through Fluid Lines. Batteries far away charge and give on paper too. When the chunk runs again, it takes on how far its record moved meanwhile.

strategy.title: One big generator far out
strategy.body: Build a [[geothermal-turbine]] beside its Wellsprings far from home and run brass on poles back to base. It powers the base without ever loading its own chunk, as long as its lava and water come in on paper too.

body.warning: No chunk is ever loaded for a network. A machine in an unloaded chunk isn't running, so it draws nothing; only generators and Batteries work on paper.

body: Networks update at most once a second, a second's worth at a time, and only while a device on them is live. Generators never wake a network on their own.

sections.title: Sizing a grid
body: Work out what your machines draw, add a margin, and pick enough generation and the right cable.

head: Fuel for
Lava
Wellsprings
rows: One Lava Wellspring with two upgrades (25 mB/s)
Two and a half Lava Generators
One Lava Wellspring with three upgrades
A Geothermal Turbine at full power
Two maxed Lava Wellsprings, and a Water Wellspring with two upgrades

strategy.title: A first machine room
strategy.body: One maxed Lava Wellspring, two Lava Generators side by side (terminals touching), a copper Power Line to an Electric Motor set to 32,768 SU, and one Battery on the line. The generators make 2,048 FE a tick, the motor takes exactly that, and the Battery carries you through a refill.

strategy.title: The grid
strategy.body: A turbine's 46,080 FE a tick runs two and a half full-power motors. Run a brass trunk on poles, feed copper branches off it at the poles, rank the branches with a [[power-splitter|power Splitter]] so the important ones come first, and hang an Industrial Battery off the trunk to cover the gaps.

name: Lines and Networks
summary: How Fluid Lines and Power Lines work: pump-free fluid, FE cable, clip-on fittings, colours, spans on poles, hiding them in walls, and what happens far away.

teach.what: The mod's own pipes and cables. [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] move fluid with no pump; [[power-lines|Power Lines]] carry FE and hang between [[line-post|Line Posts]]. Both come in copper and brass with fixed throughput, both take clip-on fittings, and both hide inside any block.
teach.why: They replace Pipez in this mod: cheaper and tidier than Create's pumps, with limits you can see and upgrades you can hold.
teach.when: Copper Fluid Lines from your first copper sheets; Power Lines with your first generator; brass once a run needs more.
teach.interacts: They connect to anything that holds fluid or FE: Create's tanks, basins and spouts, the [[fluid-wellspring]], the generators, motor and [[battery]], cages, tanks and other mods' blocks. They never join Create's Fluid Pipes.
mistakes: A Fluid Line without an [[intake]] moves nothing.
Copper and brass never join each other except at poles and Breakers, and only brass into copper.
Two colours never join; plain is a colour. Dye lines before you place them.
Lines on a moving contraption do nothing until they're placed again.

sections.title: Two kinds of line

head: Fluid Line
Power Line
rows: FE, by itself, from anything that gives it to anything that takes it
A slim round pipe with a glass window on top
A thin cable clipped flat to the floor, wall or ceiling
Hang a span between Line Posts (16 or 32 blocks)

body: Neither needs rotation, power or a pump, neither has a range limit, and neither loses anything along the way. Both come 8 to a craft.

body.fact: The fluid you see in a Fluid Line's window creeps out from the Intake and drains back when the supply stops, but that's only the look: breaking a line never spills a drop.

sections.title: Fittings
body: Upgrades aren't menu slots: they're parts you clip onto a straight piece of line, one per block. Breaking the block drops both; the Wrench takes off just the fitting.

head: Fitting
Line
What it does
Made from
rows: Draws a tank's fluid into the line; its own filter picks one fluid
Shuts on redstone; throttles in 10% steps
An upright gauge: live flow in mB a tick; comparator and Display Link source
The same gauge lying flat over the wire: live flow in FE a tick
On a straight piece: Even, Nearest first or Round robin (right-click)
On a junction: First, Second or Last per branch (Wrench screen)
Cuts power by lever or redstone; joins brass to copper

body.tip: The Intake is the one costly part, because it replaces a pump. One per source keeps a base honest without punishing long runs.

sections.title: Colours and tiers
body: Craft eight lines around a dye to colour them (16 dyes), before you place them. A dyed line is its colour all over; a dyed Power Line becomes a slightly thicker covered cable. A placed line can't be dyed; bulk washing (an Encased Fan through water) takes the dye off line items.

list: **Two colours never join**, and plain counts as a colour, so different lines can run side by side through one wall.

**Tiers never join** along a run. Copper and brass Power Lines meet only on a pole or at a [[breaker]], and there **brass feeds copper, never the other way**: the copper line takes at most its own rate.
A pole is one junction per colour, so several colours can share one row of poles.
A generator or [[battery]] joins every line that meets it into one network, whatever their colours, and serves them all.

strategy.title: Trunk and branches
strategy.body: Run a brass trunk between poles, and at each area's pole tie copper of the same colour: brass feeds each copper branch, and each branch takes up to its 4,096 FE a tick.

list: Right-click a [[line-post|Line Post]]'s insulator with Power Lines, then another post's: a span hangs between them. It uses one Power Line for every four blocks, rounded up, given back when it comes down.
Copper reaches 16 blocks, brass 32. The way between must be clear when you hang it; after that, blocks never cut it.
Spans sag gently, have no collision and never hurt anyone. Shears or the Wrench take them down.
Stack posts into a pole of any height. Right-click the top one's side with a post to add a crossarm with its own insulator, up to four.
Each insulator holds up to 2 spans, of one tier and colour.
An [[battery|Industrial Battery]]'s four corner insulators tie only to Line Posts.

body.warning: A span whose two ends move apart (a piston, a contraption, a ship flying off) comes down and drops its wire. A span with both ends on the same ship stays up and works.

sections.title: Hiding lines
body: Right-click any line with a plain, solid full block (stone, planks, casing; not glass or anything with a block entity) to encase it. The line works exactly as before, fittings and all. The block is used up from your hand, and sneak + Wrench gives it back.
With Engineer's Goggles on, hidden lines within 16 blocks show as a faint outline, and the Wrench reaches the hidden fitting first.

Run a Power Line to a solid block on each side, in the same tier and colour, and wrench one end on the side facing the block. It drills through and joins the two cable ends. Wrench again to pull it out; breaking the block fills the hole.

body.fact: Encasing your first line earns Out of Sight: "Engineer's Goggles still know where it is".

sections.title: Far away, and on the move

head: Situation
Fluid Line
Power Line
rows: Skipped: ends there get nothing; nothing is lost or queued
Reaches past it to generators beyond, which run on paper
The generator's full output still arrives, on paper
On a Create Aeronautics physics object

body: Nothing is ever chunk-loaded by a line. Power networks update at most once a second, and only while a device on them is live.

name: The Upgrade Tree
summary: Every upgrade in the mod grows from one sequenced-assembly part, the Upgrade Template: Wellspring generation and capacity upgrades on one branch, chest upgrades on the other.

teach.what: A tree of crafted parts. The [[upgrade-template]] becomes a [[drip-template]] (for the four generation upgrades), a [[capacity-upgrade]], or a [[chest-upgrade-template]] (for the five chest tiers).
teach.why: It gives you two of the most useful things early on: endless fluid from one block, and storage that holds many times more.
teach.when: From the moment you can run a sequenced assembly line with Deployers and have Electron Tubes.
teach.interacts: The [[fluid-wellspring]] takes the fluid upgrades; chests and barrels take the chest upgrades and become [[upgraded-chest|Upgraded Chests]] and [[upgraded-barrel|Barrels]].
mistakes: Mixing generation upgrades. A Wellspring takes one kind at a time (water, lava, honey or chocolate).
Installing more than three of a kind: three generation and three capacity upgrades is the maximum.
Trying to skip a chest tier: each one is built on the last.

head: From
Add (sequenced assembly)
Makes
rows: 3 loops: Honeycomb Block, 1,000 mB honey, Precision Mechanism, press
3 loops: Cocoa Beans, 1,000 mB chocolate, Precision Mechanism, press

sections.title: Wellspring upgrades
body: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with an upgrade to install it; a Wrench opens its upgrade screen to add or remove them. Each generation upgrade plugs into a socket on the lid; each Capacity Upgrade is a canister in the lid's back row.
The tank holds 8,000 mB, plus 16,000 mB for each Capacity Upgrade (56,000 mB with three).

body.tip: Honey and chocolate meet lava as limestone and scoria (Create's own fluid interactions), so a Honey or Chocolate Wellspring beside a Lava one is an endless source of either stone.

body.warning: To switch a Wellspring to another fluid, empty it of the old one first. A Capacity Upgrade can't come out until the tank is drained to what the smaller tank holds.

body.fact: Three generation upgrades in one Wellspring earn Maximum Overdrip: "Turn it up to eleven! (Well, three)".

sections.title: Chest upgrades

head: Tier
Made from
Items per slot
Slots
rows: Chest Upgrade Template + 2 copper sheets, pressed
Smithing: Netherite Upgrade template + Diamond upgrade + netherite ingot

body: Using a higher tier on an upgraded chest hands back the old upgrade, so climbing the ladder never wastes one. Counts are for 64-stack items; unstackable items stay at one a slot.

strategy.title: One template line, many finishers
strategy.body: Run a sequenced assembly line that only makes Upgrade Templates, and send them to short second lines: one with two Pointed Dripstone deployers and a Spout for water or lava, one with three Fluid Tank deployers, one with a chest and Andesite Alloy. Each finisher is a few Deployers on a belt.

body.tip: The honey and chocolate upgrades eat three Precision Mechanisms each. Make those on their own line first, or the upgrade line will stall.

name: One-Block Farming
summary: The Auto Harvester, Animal Pens, Monster Cages and Fish Tanks: whole farms in one block, sharing one set of rules for power, culling, output and automation.

teach.what: Four families of farm block. The [[auto-harvester]] grows and harvests one plant; the [[animal-pen]] breeds a herd from one bottled animal; the [[monster-cage]] brings in a horde of one jarred monster; the [[fish-tank]] breeds a school underwater. Each is a Create-style box with the real creatures or plant behind the glass.
teach.why: They replace sprawling farms with one block each, safely, with vanilla drops and vanilla rates, and every step can be automated with Create parts.
teach.when: The Harvester, Animal Pen, Monster Cage and Fish Tank are all early to mid game (andesite alloy and Andesite Casing); their Brass versions follow with Mechanical Crafting.
teach.interacts: Their drops feed the rest of the base: string and slime for the [[string-tangler]], wheat for [[monster-chow|Monster Chow]] and [[fish-food|Fish Food]], milk, wool, eggs, ink and fish. Enchantments speed them up: [[bountiful]], [[fruitful]] and [[monstrous]].
mistakes: Expecting more speed to help the Harvester or the pens. They use a fixed stress and run no faster; only the cages and tanks scale with RPM.
Forgetting the food. Pens, cages and tanks only grow while they have food (and water, for tanks and Flooded cages).
Using the wrong catcher. Animals and water creatures go in a [[capture-bottle]], monsters in an [[iron-jar]], the Wither in a [[netherite-jar]].
Taking the bottle or jar out to tidy up. That empties the block: the rest are culled into the output.

head: Block
Holds
Start with
Feed
Power
Enchantment
rows: A bottled fish, squid or axolotl

sections.title: Shared rules

list: Power goes into a shaft in the **back**.
**No stress while idle**: empty, full, out of food or water, or overstressed, the block puts no load on the network.

Output goes into slots (9, or 18 on the Brass blocks; nine stacks on the Harvester) that hoppers, chutes, funnels and arms empty from any side, or you empty by hand. A full Harvester stops; a cage or tank throws what doesn't fit out of its front.
A **Wrench** opens the screen: the plant, bottle or jar, the food, gauges, the output and the count, with quick-move buttons and the mouse wheel on the output.
Taking the bottle or jar out empties the block: the others are culled into the output.
Pens, cages and tanks grow nothing while their chunk is unloaded. On a contraption they ride along with their contents, without working.
Only empty cages and tanks can be upgraded (Andesite to Brass, dry to Flooded, Fish Tank to Brass Fish Tank).

body: The Auto Harvester and the Animal Pens use a **fixed stress** and run no faster for more speed: a crop takes 40 seconds (scaled by its vanilla growth rate), a tree 80, and pens breed every five minutes, as in vanilla. The Monster Cages and Fish Tanks **scale with speed**: 64 RPM is the base, faster shafts are linearly quicker, and stress and food use rise with them.

sections.title: Culling with swords
body: Use a sword on a pen, cage or tank to cull **half** the adults (rounded), always leaving one. The drops come from the creature's own loot table as if you'd killed it, so **Looting** and **Fire Aspect** count, and you get its XP.

list: A **Deployer** with a sword culls the same way, but gives no XP.
The young are left to grow up; only adults breed and give drops, wool, eggs or milk.
Culling with one left does nothing.
Armed drowned are culled first; blue axolotls last.

body.tip: A Fire Aspect sword cooks the meat from a pen of cows or pigs as it culls.

body.fact: Taking a sword to a pen earns Thinning the Herd.

head: Job
Create part
rows: Shear sheep, take milk, scoop fish
A Deployer with shears, a bucket or a water bucket
Deployers and Dispensers with Capture Bottles and Iron Jars (a Dispenser never releases a Wither)
Funnels, chutes or arms into any side
Funnels, chutes, hoppers or arms from any side
Pipes or [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] on any side but the back
A comparator reads how full of creatures it is; on cages and tanks, Display Links show count, status and water

strategy.title: A self-running cage
strategy.body: A Deployer with a sword on a clock in front of a [[monster-cage]], a funnel pulling the drops into an [[upgraded-chest]], and a second funnel pushing Monster Chow in from a Mixer line. A comparator on the cage can trigger the Deployer only when the horde is nearly full.

sections.title: Balanced against vanilla
body: Every cull rolls the vanilla loot table at vanilla rates, evokers' Totems included. The blocks change how often creatures come, never what they drop. Pens breed and grow on vanilla's own clock.
What limits them is cost: food for every birth, Monster Chow for every arrival (1, 2, 4 or 64 depending on the monster), water, stress, and the price of the Brass and Netherite tiers.

body.fact: A good vanilla mob farm still out-produces a Monster Cage. The cage wins on space, safety and automation: it replaces a farm, not a resource.

name: Farm Enchantments
summary: Bountiful, Fruitful and Monstrous: three anvil-only enchantments, bought from Librarians, that speed up the one-block farms by 50% a level.

teach.what: Three enchantments, each I to III, each for its own machines: [[bountiful]] on the [[auto-harvester]], [[fruitful]] on the Animal Pens and Fish Tanks, [[monstrous]] on every Monster Cage. Each level adds 50% speed: 1.5x, 2x, 2.5x.
teach.why: The Harvester and pens run no faster for more rotation, so these are their only speed-up. On cages and tanks they're extra speed without extra stress.
teach.when: As soon as you have a farm block and a village with a Librarian.
teach.interacts: They go on the machine's item with an anvil and stay on it when the block is broken and placed again. Faster farms eat their food or chow faster.
mistakes: Looking in an enchanting table. They're never offered there.
Putting one on the wrong machine. The anvil refuses: each fits only its own family.
Forgetting the food bill. Fruitful and Monstrous speed up eating as well as breeding.

head: Enchantment
Goes on
Speeds up
Advancement
rows: The plant's growth (the 4-second harvest stays the same)
Animal Pen, Brass Animal Pen, Fish Tank, Brass Fish Tank
Be Fruitful and Multiply (a pen with Fruitful III)
Every Monster Cage, the Netherite one included

sections.title: Getting the books
body: Librarians sell them, two ways:

list: In their **usual random enchanted-book trades**, alongside vanilla's books.

As **extra Apprentice trades**: a book of each of the three joins the Apprentice trade pool, at a random level from I to III, for emeralds and a book, priced like the Librarian's own enchanted books. A Librarian reaching Apprentice may draw one of them.

body: Two books of the same level combine on an anvil into the next level, as vanilla books do.

body.tip: Trade with a Librarian until it reaches Apprentice and check its new offers. If it hasn't got the one you want, another Librarian might.

sections.title: Putting them on

list: Combine the book with the machine's item on an anvil.
Break the block and place it again: the enchantment stays.
The machine's screen (and on tanks, goggles) shows its level.

body.warning: Speed costs food. A Fruitful III pen eats 2.5 times as fast, and a Monstrous III cage of blazes eats Monster Chow 2.5 times as fast. Keep the feed line ahead of it.

body: The bonus per level is in the server config for each family.

name: Stone Generation
summary: One-block cobblestone, basalt, blackstone and tuff generators, paced like a Mechanical Drill, and what each stone feeds in the rest of the mod.

teach.what: Shaft-driven boxes where water or ice meets lava and a drill mines the stone that forms. The [[cobblestone-generator]], [[basalt-generator]] and [[blackstone-generator]] come in Andesite, Brass and Wireless versions; the [[tuff-generator]] in plain and Wireless.
teach.why: Stone is the raw material of the dust lines: crushed cobblestone gives [[emerald-dust]], netherrack made from it gives [[netherite-dust]], blackstone gives [[quartz-dust]], tuff gives metal nuggets for the [[stone-infuser]].
teach.when: Very early: the Andesite generator needs only Andesite Alloy, two drills, casing and a bucket of each fluid (the buckets come back).
teach.interacts: Output leaves only through item transport (hoppers, chutes, funnels, Pipez, arms) from any side. A redstone signal (or a Redstone Link frequency on a Wireless one) switches it off with no stress.
mistakes: Putting the shaft in the side. Power only goes in through the shaft hole on the back.
Waiting for it to drop stone on the floor. It only gives stone to item transport; full, it stops.
Building a Brass generator with no crusher behind it: 16 a cycle fills a slow line fast.

sections.title: The generators
body: A cycle takes exactly as long as a Mechanical Drill at the same speed takes to mine that block, so softer stones come faster.
Each has a **Wireless** version: craft it with a Transmitter. It gets an antenna with two frequency slots, set like a Redstone Link; a signal on that frequency switches it off. It's permanent.

list: A shaft into the back hole is its only power input.
A lamp on the front frame shows its state: cyan running, amber full, dark red switched off by redstone, unlit with no rotation.
Full or switched off, it stops and puts no stress on the network.
Breaking it drops what it holds.
Goggles show how much it holds and its output per minute.

body.tip: Use a redstone signal, or a Wireless frequency, to stop a generator when its storage is full instead of letting it back up: it then costs nothing.

Into
Gives

A Mixer, heated, with 20 gold nuggets
Gilded Blackstone (crushing it gives 18 nuggets back)
A few of all four nuggets, to feed the Stone Infuser

body.warning: The Stone Infuser can't loop into free metal: crushing its stones always gives back fewer than the 9 nuggets they took.

name: Precious Dusts
summary: Emerald, Netherite and Quartz Dust from crushing stone, pressed in the Pressure Crucible into Emeralds, Netherite Scrap and Nether Quartz.

teach.what: Create's Crushing Wheels and Millstones now leave rare dusts behind: [[emerald-dust]] from cobblestone and stone, [[netherite-dust]] and [[quartz-dust]] from netherrack, and more quartz from blackstone. The [[pressure-crucible]] presses them into gems and scrap over a Blaze Burner.
teach.why: Fully automatable emeralds, netherite and quartz from cobblestone and lava, with no villagers, no ancient debris and no Nether trips.
teach.when: Emerald Dust from your first Crushing Wheels; the Crucible once you have brass and obsidian; netherite once you can keep a burner superheated with Blaze Cakes.
teach.interacts: [[stone-generation|Stone generators]] supply the stone; a [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]] supplies the lava for netherrack. The same netherrack crushing gives cinder flour for [[monster-chow|Monster Chow]].
mistakes: Pressing over the wrong heat. Emeralds and Nether Quartz need heated; Netherite Scrap, amethyst, obsidian and diamonds need superheated.
Under-sizing the crushers. The chances are small; it's a volume game.
Starving the Crucible of stress. It takes 12 SU per RPM, so 3,072 SU at 256 RPM.

sections.title: Where dust comes from

head: Crushed
Machine
Main output
Dust
rows: Cinder flour (1, plus 50% for a second)

body: Netherrack comes from a Mixer over a **heated** Blaze Burner: cobblestone and 50 mB of lava.

body.fact: These are ordinary data-pack recipes, so pack makers can change every chance, count and time. JEI and Create's own recipe pages show them.

sections.title: Pressing it
body: The [[pressure-crucible]] sits on a Blaze Burner and takes rotation through a shaft into its back. Right-click with dust to load it, with an empty hand to take results out; funnels, hoppers and pipes do both from any side.
At 64 RPM an Emerald takes 2.5 seconds and a Netherite Scrap 10; glass and stone take half a second each, and diamonds are slow.
It presses faster at higher speeds: 16 RPM is the base, 256 RPM is 16 times as fast. Goggles show the contents, the heat needed, progress and what's holding it up.

head: Result
On average, it takes
rows: About 900 netherrack crushed: 900 cobblestone and 45,000 mB of lava

strategy.title: Feeding a netherite line
strategy.body: A Brass [[cobblestone-generator]] makes 16 cobblestone a cycle. Split it: some to Crushing Wheels for Emerald Dust, the rest to a heated Mixer fed lava from a maxed [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]] (50 mB/s is lava for one netherrack a second), then on to a second pair of Crushing Wheels. Netherite, quartz and cinder flour all come off that one crusher.

name: Create Aeronautics
summary: What the mod adds for Create Aeronautics ships: the Compact Gyroscope, Torque Rotor and Flight Instruments, Aviator's Goggles in the Curios slot, and Pipez feeding Portable Engines.

teach.what: Three ship blocks (only present with Sable, Create Aeronautics' physics): the [[compact-gyroscope]] keeps a ship level, the [[torque-rotor]] turns it without sideways drift, and [[flight-instruments]] read altitude, airspeed, attitude and heading. Plus goggles in the Curios head slot and pipe-fed Portable Engines.
teach.why: Ships drift, wobble and need refuelling. These make them steadier, easier to steer and easier to keep running.
teach.when: Once you're flying, and have Precision Mechanisms.
teach.interacts: Most of the mod keeps working on Aeronautics physics objects: Wellsprings, upgraded chests and barrels, the generators, the [[magma-engine]], the [[pressure-crucible]], Fluid and Power Lines, and the Monster Cages.
mistakes: Looking for the gyroscope, rotor or instruments without Sable installed. They only exist with it.
Expecting the Torque Rotor to push the ship along. It turns it; use propellers to move.
Placing the Flight Instruments facing the wrong way. The way you face it counts as forward.

sections.title: Staying level
body: The [[compact-gyroscope]] is the Gyroscope Stabilizers' Gyroscope in one block, running the same controller with the same default strength, damping and lean correction. Its gimbal swings so the flywheel stays level with the world while the ship tilts round it.

list: It reaches full strength at 256 RPM.
A redstone signal brakes it: the stronger the signal, the slower it spins and the less it holds the ship; a full signal stops it (the shaft keeps turning).
With Gyroscope Stabilizers installed, craft their Gyroscope on its own to convert it, and turn a Compact one back the same way.
Goggles show its spin, how hard it's correcting and the ship's tilt.

body.tip: A lever on the gyroscope is an easy off switch for when you want the ship free to tilt; flip it back and the ship levels out again.

sections.title: Steering without drift
body: The [[torque-rotor]] pushes the way its blades face (or pulls, with the shaft reversed), exactly as hard as an Andesite Propeller at the same speed. The ship turns just as it would from a propeller in that spot, but it isn't pushed along, so there's no sideways drift.

strategy.title: A tail rotor
strategy.body: Mount it on the tail, facing sideways, to yaw the ship. The further from the middle, the harder it turns. Reverse the shaft to turn the other way.

body: It mounts on the face you click, with the shaft going into its base, and blows wind like a propeller.

sections.title: Knowing where you are
body: [[flight-instruments|Flight Instruments]] have an altimeter (long hand per 100 m, short per 1,000 m), airspeed (0 to 60 m/s), an artificial horizon that tilts with roll and drops with pitch, and heading. Goggles show every reading, and Display Links can put altitude, airspeed, climb rate, heading or pitch and roll on Display Boards and Nixie Tubes, refreshed every second.

sections.title: Goggles and fuel

body.heading: Aviator's Goggles in the Curios slot

body: With Curios installed, wear Aviator's Goggles in the head slot, over a helmet if you like. They still count as goggles for Create's overlays. Client settings choose whether they show in the slot and over helmets.

With Pipez, item pipes feed coal and other burnable items into Portable Engines, and fluid pipes feed lava and other fuel fluids (any fluid whose bucket burns). 1,000 mB gives the same burn time as a bucket, and engines are topped up to one bucket's worth at a time.

body.tip: A [[magma-engine]] on the ship, fed by a Lava Wellspring, gives four Portable Engines' worth of power without refuelling. Its recipe uses Aeronautics' Engine Assembly.

body.warning: A [[netherite-monster-cage]] works on an airship with real rotation and FE, and if the ship's power fails, Withers escape in mid-air.

body.fact: Wearing the goggles in the Curios slot earns Goggle-Eyed Ace: "Your helmet's free and you look fabulous".

name: Readouts
summary: How to see what every block is doing: Engineer's Goggles, Display Links, comparators, Ponder scenes and JEI.

teach.what: Every block in the mod reports its state the Create way. Engineer's Goggles show live details, Display Links put numbers on boards, comparators turn fill levels into redstone, and Ponder scenes (hold **W** over an item) teach how each block works.
teach.why: Long lines, far generators and sealed farms are hard to check by eye. Readouts tell you what's wrong before it stops your base.
teach.when: From day one: Engineer's Goggles are cheap, and Ponder is free.
teach.interacts: Comparator outputs drive Create's redstone (Valves, Breakers, clutches, Deployers); Display Links feed Display Boards and Nixie Tubes.
mistakes: Flying blind on power. Goggles on any generator, machine or wire show the whole network's supply and demand.
Forgetting that a Meter's comparator signal is a fraction of the line's own throughput, not an amount.

body.tip: A comparator on a cage into a Deployer's redstone makes it cull only when the horde is nearly full, saving sword durability.

sections.title: Ponder and JEI
body: Hold **W** over an item for its Ponder scene. Scenes cover the Wellspring, chest and barrel upgrades, Pressure Crucible, every stone generator, both Magma Engines, Incinerator, String Tangler, Stone Infuser, Fluid Lines, fittings, Power Lines and Power Networks, the Lava Generator, Electric Motor, Geothermal Turbine, Battery and Industrial Battery, the Auto Harvester, Animal Pens, Monster Cages (dry, Flooded and Containment), Fish Tanks, the Cuckoo Clock, and Trade Bot (his station, linking and trading). With Sable: the Compact Gyroscope, Torque Rotor and Flight Instruments.
JEI shows the Crucible, tangling and infusing recipes and the dust chances on Create's crushing and milling pages, with info pages for the Fluid and Power Lines, the Line Post and every fitting.

name: Compatibility
summary: How the mod behaves on Create contraptions and Aeronautics ships, and with Carry On, Pipez, Curios and modded crops.

teach.what: Almost everything in the mod survives being moved: on Create contraptions, on Create Aeronautics physics objects, and in Carry On's hands. It also works with Pipez, Curios and modded crops.
teach.why: Create bases move. Knowing what keeps working on a train or a ship, and what only rides along, saves you from losing a farm or a tank of lava.
teach.when: Whenever you put a block on something that moves, or add another mod.
teach.interacts: Contraptions carry blocks and their contents; Aeronautics ships run them for real, with real rotation and FE.
mistakes: Expecting a Pressure Crucible to press on a Create contraption. It needs real rotation, so on a contraption it just rides along; on an Aeronautics ship it works.
Trying to carry Trade Bot's station or the Netherite Monster Cage with Carry On. Both are blocked.
Expecting Fluid and Power Lines to work on a moving contraption. They pause until placed again.

sections.title: Create Aeronautics physics objects
body: The Wellspring, upgraded chests and barrels, the stone generators, the Magma Engines, the Pressure Crucible, the Monster Cages and Fluid and Power Lines keep working and keep their contents when a ship is assembled and disassembled. Spans with both ends on the same ship stay up.

body.warning: A Netherite Monster Cage on a ship needs its FE in flight. If the ship's power fails, Withers escape in mid-air.

sections.title: Carry On
body: Wellsprings, upgraded chests and barrels, Batteries (with their charge), and the Andesite and Brass cages, pens and tanks can be carried and placed back with their contents.

list: Sneak + empty hand is Carry On's pickup, which is why the mod's upgrade screens open with a Wrench.

Place a carried upgraded chest against the side of a matching single one to join them into a double. Picking up half of a double moves the upgrade to whichever half needs it, and is refused if neither half would fit a vanilla chest.
Trade Bot (and his station), the Netherite Monster Cage and the Cuckoo Clock's weights are on Carry On's blacklist.
Item pipes can feed fuel into Blaze Burners (works alongside Create: Liquid Fuel). By default hoppers and funnels can too; a config option limits it to Pipez only.

With Create Aeronautics, item pipes feed coal and other burnables into Portable Engines, and fluid pipes feed lava and other fuel fluids (1,000 mB burns as long as a bucket; engines top up to one bucket's worth).
Pipez energy pipes connect to the generators, motor and Trade Bot's station like any FE cable.
[[pipez-covers|Pipez Covers]] are retired: placed ones keep working, but they can't be crafted. Use [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] and [[power-lines|Power Lines]], which encase in any block.

body.fact: Feeding a Blaze Burner through a Pipez pipe earns Pipe Dreams; piping lava into a Portable Engine earns Liquid Courage.

list: **Curios**: Aviator's Goggles go in the head slot, over a helmet if you like, and still count as goggles for Create's overlays.

**Modded crops**: any crop built on vanilla's crop or bush blocks grows in the [[auto-harvester]] with its own drops, stages and model (Supplementaries' flax, Farmer's Delight's cabbages and onions). Two-block crops show both halves.
**Modded animals and monsters**: the [[capture-bottle]] takes any animal that breeds; modded monsters go in the Brass cage at 2 Monster Chow each.
**Inventory Profiles Next** is kept off upgraded chest screens, because it simulates vanilla stack sizes; the mod's own quick moves replace it there.
**Create Seats**: villagers and wandering traders sit on them properly, legs bent, also on moving contraptions. That's what [[trade-bot|Trade Bot]] looks for.

name: Configuration
summary: What you can change, and where: the in-game config screen, its server and client sections, and the data-pack recipes and tags behind the mod.

teach.what: Nearly every number on this site is a default. Server settings cover rates, capacities, stress, FE and the Wither escapes; client settings cover how goggles look in the Curios slot. Recipes and the lists of what goes where are data packs and tags.
teach.why: So a server or modpack can tune the mod to its own balance without code.
teach.when: When you run a server, build a pack, or find a number that doesn't suit your world.
teach.interacts: Server settings apply to everyone in the world and can be edited while in it. Data packs change recipes, dust chances and which monsters go in which cage.
mistakes: Changing client settings and expecting other players to see it: they're yours alone.
Reading this site's numbers on a modded server. A pack may have changed them: Engineer's Goggles and JEI show the real values.

sections.title: Where to find it
body: In game: **Mods, Create, Config, Access configs of other mods, ComedyMonkey's Create Addons**. Server settings can be edited while you're in a world.
On disk they're NeoForge config files: the server file lives with the world, the client file in your game's config folder.

list: **Recipes** are ordinary data-pack recipes: the Crucible's (dust, heat, time), the dust chances on Create's crushing and milling, the String Tangler's `comedymonkeysaddons:tangling` and the Stone Infuser's `comedymonkeysaddons:infusing`.
**Auto Harvester**: item tags `comedymonkeysaddons:auto_harvester_plantable` and `auto_harvester_blacklist` add or forbid plants.

**Monster Cages**: entity tags `monster_cage/andesite`, `/brass`, `/rare`, `/netherite`, `/flooded` and `/blacklist` decide which cage takes a monster and its chow cost. Any monster not in a tag counts as Brass.
**Pens and tanks**: entity tags `pen_blacklist` and `fish_tank_blacklist` keep creatures out.

name: Clockwork Ruins
summary: Rings of broken walls, five chunks across, that grow taller and closer the further in you go. Something kneels at the middle. It is not a statue.

sections.title: Finding them
body: They lie on dry land in the Overworld (forests, plains, taiga, savanna, snow, desert, swamp, hills) and on the End's outer islands, about one in every 64 by 64 chunks in the Overworld and one in 48 by 48 in the End, never close to a village or an End city.

At the edge you notice only the odd fallen block. Walk inward and there are stubs of wall, then broken walls with vines on them, then tall ragged corners and heaps of rubble, with brass and old shafting among them. At the middle stands a roofless hall.

sections.title: The hall
body: A chest in the back corner holds brass, zinc, Andesite Alloy, cogwheels and a Precision Mechanism or three.

body.warning: Something kneels on the dais. Come close and it begins to wake.

sections.title: In the End
body: The same hall in End Stone and purpur, half sunk into its island, with chorus growing where the vines would be.

gallery.caption: The hall at the middle, its dais empty for now
